cobham.heading: Political gardening
cobham.about:
Back in the 1700s Lord Cobham had strong views and ambitious plans which head gardener Barry Smith helps us find out with a wander around the garden.
Stowe Gardens website

river_rinse.heading: Rinsing a river
river_rinse.about:
It's September in Buckingham which means it's time to get the river back in shape and Mayor Fran Davies tells us how they do it.
Buckingham Events

buckingham_chantry_chapel.heading: Chanted to heaven
buckingham_chantry_chapel.about:
How did a medieval fast-track to heaven for the rich become a route for educating the poor?
Buckingham Chantry Chapel

buckingham_gaol.heading: Buckingham Old Gaol
buckingham_gaol.about:
Jo Thompson, Chair of Buckingham Old Gaol Trust takes us for a wander around the town's museum.
Buckingham Old Gaol

buckingham_canal_society.heading: Reviving a canal
buckingham_canal_society.about: Athena Beckett takes time out from managing a volunteer work party to tell us about the work of the Buckingham Canal Society.

bluetits.heading: Sunday swarm
bluetits.about:
It's a nippy Sunday morning in Stony Straford which means it's time to join the local Bluetits swarm for a swim.
Milton Keynes Bluetits

bard_of_stony.heading: Bard of Stony
bard_of_stony.about:
Nova Carmen, Bard of Stony Stratford, shares some tips and a poem to help us get creative on the long walk to Kings Lynn.
Bard of Stony Stratford

parks_trust.heading: In parks we trust
parks_trust.about:
Ellie Durrant tells us about the Parks Trust's new plans for developing their Wetland Arc.
Parks Trust

bradwell_abbey.heading: A place of pilgrimage
bradwell_abbey.about:
The new city of Milton Keynes contains some ancient gems including St Mary's Chapel. Camille Poole shows us around.
website

bradwell_windmill.heading: Feeding from afar
bradwell_windmill.about:
Richard Wilde from Milton Keynes museum tells us what an old windmill is doing in a new city and the clue is the canal-side setting...
Website

passivhaus.heading: Passivhaus
passivhaus.about:
A wander through Manor Park might take you back in time to the Georgian era, but it's a place where Alan Budden and his colleagues are designing housing of the future.
Eco Design Consultants

kerrys_way.heading: Kerry's Way
kerrys_way.about:
Let's go for a wander with Kerry Thompson and find out how she is helping to make parks accessible for all of us.
My life, Kerry's Way

cowper_newton_museum.heading: Amazing Grace
cowper_newton_museum.about:
Why do people come from around the globe to visit this museum and then sing a hymn in the local church? Tom Jones helps us find out why.
Cowper & Newton Museum

emmaus.heading: A home for all
emmaus.about:
It's a charity, a community and a popular place to have a break. I speak to Operations Manager, Lynn Reeves to find out more.
Emmaus website

harrold_odell_country_park.heading: Harrold Odell Park
harrold_odell_country_park.about: It's been called the jewel of North Bedfordshire and the Ouse Valley Way passes right through it. I meet Ed Green who shares with us how he keeps this local gem in good order. Park website

john_bunyan.heading: A Pilgrim's Progress
john_bunyan.about:
Between Pavenham and Bromham Mill, the Ouse Valley Way joins another walking route - The John Bunyan Trail. I met with John Pestell from the Bunyan Museum to find out more about the man and his greatest work.
Bunyan Museum

guru_nanak_temple.heading: Guru Nanak Gurdwara
guru_nanak_temple.about:
There's an impressive temple visible from the Ouse Valley Way. Let's go visit it and learn some lessons for people of all faiths and none.
Facebook page

la_piazza.heading: A taste of Italy
la_piazza.about:
Let's talk to Libby, owner of La Piazza cafe and find out more about Bedford's Italian connection.
website

panacea.heading: 20th Century Preppers
panacea.about:
What would you do if an Apocalypse was imminent? Museum director, Zara Matthews, shows us what one incredible group of ladies decided to do.
Panacea Museum

higgins.heading: Remembering the R101
higgins.about:
Why did the R101's maiden flight end in tragedy? Lydia McDonald, Keeper of Social History at the Higgins, helps us find out. She also shows us why Bedford was a centre for innovation that made it the place to build airships.
Website

roxtonchapel.heading: Roxton Chapel
roxtonchapel.about:
Richard Hooker shows us around a chapel that used to have a very different purpose.
Chapel Website

roxtonchapelbonus.heading: Roxton Chapel bonus
roxtonchapelbonus.about: If you are curious to know what the wonderful organ at Roxton Chapel sounds like, Richard has very kindly agreed to record and share a selection of hymns with us.

paxton_pits.heading: Paxton Pits
paxton_pits.about:
Paxton Pits Ranger, Robyn Staddon takes us to a bird hide to discover the special things to see and hear in the nature reserve.
Paxton Pits

buckden_towers.heading: Buckden Towers
buckden_towers.about:
Frances Farmer takes us on a tour of a place where Catherine of Aragon has made a big impression.
Friends of Buckden Towers

cromwell_museum.heading: Warts and all
cromwell_museum.about:
Curator Stuart Orme takes us around the Cromwell Museum to learn about one of England's most consequential and controversial figures in history.
Cromwell Museum

govt.heading: This is the Way
govt.about: What does it take to get the Ouse Valley Way in good shape? Graham Campbell tells us about the fantastic work of the Great Ouse Valley Trust in improving the Huntingdonshire stretch and their ambitious plans for the future.

citizenscience.heading: Citizen Science
citizenscience.about:
Let's join Lucas Tatek who regularly tests the river checking for harmful bacteria at a popular paddling place.
find a citizen science group
Environment Agency

watermills.heading: The missing mill detectives
watermills.about:
On a stretch of river that was a powerhouse of watermilling, Keith Grimwade and Bridget Flannagan have done a deep dive into the history and landscape to find the missing mills.
Book details

hartford_marina.heading: Hartford Marina
hartford_marina.about:
The Ouse Valley Way passes Hartford Marina. Let's go talk to Max and find out more about boating.
Website

holt_island.heading: Holt, who goes there?
holt_island.about:
Let's go on a tour of Holt Island with Keith Grimwade to find out more about the nature reserve that used to be a hive of industry.
Holt Island

norris.heading: A lasting legacy
norris.about:
When avid collector Herbert Norris died in 1931, he left his collection of Huntingdonshire artifacts to St Ives. Richard Carter takes us on a guided tour and shows us how people today are learning about Huntingdonshire.
Norris Museum

rspb_ouse_fen.heading: Building a habitat
rspb_ouse_fen.about:
A project is underway turning quarried land into a unique reserve based on reedbeds. Let's talk to the wardens Richard Taylor and Ian Weller to find out more.
RSPB Ouse Fen

stretham_old_engine.heading: Keeping farming afloat
stretham_old_engine.about:
The Fens are Britain's bread-basket thanks to pumping stations keeping the land drained. Volunteer Nick Sharpe shows us how Stretham Old Engine has been helping keep the country fed.
Museum website

stained_glass_museum.heading: The art of glass
stained_glass_museum.about:
Most of the churches along the Ouse Valley Way contain treasures hiding in plain sight - stained glass. Emily Allen from the Stained Glass Museum is going to help us see what we have been looking through.
Museum website

cromwells_house.heading: Cromwell's House
cromwells_house.about:
An obvious place to start any visit to Ely is at the tourist information office and it comes with an added bonus - it was also Oliver Cromwell’s family home which Anna Bennett shows us around.
Website

downham.heading: The Gingerbread Trail
downham.about:
Discover Downham volunteer, Kathleen Wiseman, takes us on a tour of Downham to find out why it's known as the Gingerbread Town. It's also a chance to meet the dedicated volunteers who have been determined to save the artifacts and share the stories of their town.
Discover Downham

hanse.heading: A league of gentlemensch
hanse.about:
We're in a couryard where in medieval times people would have been talking German. Let's talk to Dr Paul Richards to find out why.
Hanse House
